title: Journey Mapper Contract
description: Contract for modules/journey_mapper, implemented in 11_Benchmark_Engine/modules/journey_mapper/. Journey Mapper is a planning engine only: it never navigates, clicks, or uses Playwright. Given a Discovery Report, an optional UI Map, and a homepage screenshot path (referenced only, not pixel-analyzed), it produces a JourneyPlan — an ordered, reasoned sequence of journey steps a future Navigation Runner (Sprint 10) should attempt, why, and how confident this module is in each. Not wired into the orchestrator yet.

Confidence.description: Matches analysis.schema.json#/$defs/Confidence and discovery.schema.json#/$defs/Confidence — the same three-value vocabulary used everywhere in this Engine.

PriorityTier.description: 1 = AI-first experience, 2 = Trip Planning/personalization, 3 = Search, 4 = Booking, 5 = everything else. Fixed ranking this module optimizes for, per the platform's AI-first mandate.

UIMapElement.description: Mirrors the UI Map element shape designed alongside Discovery (id, label, role, element_type, locator_strategy, href, clickable, visible, confidence, bounding_box, parent_section, related_journey_step). No module produces this yet — Journey Mapper accepts it as an optional enrichment input and degrades gracefully to text-only reasoning when it is absent, recording that as an explicit assumption rather than guessing locators itself.

discovery_report.description: Consumed directly as Discovery's output type — no separate transport format.

ui_map.description: Optional. Empty/absent until a UI Map producer exists — see UIMapElement.

screenshot_path.description: Optional. Referenced for traceability only — this module does not analyze image content.

title.description: Short, human-readable label for this step.

goal.description: What evidence this step is meant to gather.

reason.description: Why this step was included — cites the Discovery/UI Map evidence behind it.

expected_result.description: What a successful capture at this step should look like.

depends_on_previous.description: True if this step only makes sense after another already-planned step succeeded (e.g. booking after search).

possible_failure.description: How this step could fail to produce evidence, so the Navigation Runner knows what to watch for.

affects.description: Which step id(s) this blocker affects, or 'all steps until resolved'.

trigger.description: The condition under which the Navigation Runner should switch to this path.

sequence.description: Step ids (or a recovery action id) in fallback order.

starting_url.description: Discovery's resolved_url — the already-established entry point; not itself a planned step.

primary_goal.description: One-line statement of what this journey is optimizing to learn first.

confidence.description: Overall confidence in this plan as a whole — never higher than its weakest planned step.

recommended_first_action.description: The single next thing the orchestrator/Navigation Runner should do.

recommended_journey.description: Ordered by priority tier, then by confidence. Only includes steps with actual Discovery evidence (applicable_guess: true) — this module does not fabricate steps it has no evidence for.

assumptions.description: Explicit list of what this plan assumes due to missing or partial input (no UI Map, copy-only AI evidence, no screenshot, etc.).
